answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via Proof-of-Replication with space-time audits. Each node seals a unique gigabyte-scale sector bound to its key via a sequential hash graph and answers random Merkle challenges per epoch, stopping clones from hollowing the registry like karst. Keeping this haven sturdy as cedar forces attackers to dedicate disk capacity and IOPS per identity rather than free keys. However, storage farms can still fund extra slots, and thin agents face steep overhead.
